messages:
ash_customer: Hey team — we're seeing intermittent 429s and large tail latencies on /v1/generate this morning around 2026-03-15 17:02–17:10 UTC. Example request-id: req_6b8c3f2a. Response headers included X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset: 1647343872. Can you advise what to collect to repro?

alex_support: Sorry about that — we'll take it. First ask: can you paste a minimal curl that reproduces it (with any auth redacted) and the exact request-id you saw? Also ZIP up any client-side logs if possible.

ash_customer: Here's the curl we used (token replaced):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Client-Request-Id: req_6b8c3f2a" \n  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"Summarize monthly billing"}'
```
We also have a HAR from the client and a short tcpdump if you want.

maria_sre: Thanks. Please upload the HAR + a debug bundle (curl --trace-ascii or tcpdump) to the ticket. In parallel can you run a quick replay with our debug header so we can correlate on the gateway? Example: add `-H "X-Debug-Trace: enable"` to the curl. That will cause our gateway to emit a trace id.

ash_customer: OK starting a run now with debug header, will attach results. I ran three sequential requests at 17:03:05, 17:03:06, 17:03:07 UTC and got 429 on the 3rd. New request-ids: req_6b8c3f2a, req_6b8c3f2b, req_6b8c3f2c.

alex_support: Good — can you also capture response headers for each (especially X-RateLimit-* and X-Backend-Node / X-Req-Route if present)? A text snippet is fine.

ash_customer: Pasted snippets: 
- req_6b8c3f2a -> X-RateLimit-Remaining: 5, X-RateLimit-Limit: 10
- req_6b8c3f2b -> X-RateLimit-Remaining: 1
- req_6b8c3f2c -> HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, Retry-After: 2

sam_eng: Noted. Maria — could this be a bursting/pacing policy mismatch? They show quick sequential calls. We should check per-minute window and the proxy per-client token limit.

maria_sre: I'll pull the gateway logs for those request-ids. replay-bot: start replay for req_6b8c3f2a, req_6b8c3f2b, req_6b8c3f2c

replay-bot: Enqueued replay job id rjob_0042. Will run against staging routing table.

maria_sre: From initial logs: gateway enforced quota at node gw-03 at 2026-03-15T17:03:07Z, client_token: cust_42, rate_window=60s, remaining_before=1. It looks like their client made 3 rapid requests and hit the per-minute hard limit. Attaching snippet: 
```
[gw-03] 2026-03-15T17:03:07.123Z INFO request=req_6b8c3f2c action=reject reason=rate_limit remaining=0 limit=10 window=60s
```

alex_support: That log line helps. ash_customer, do you batch or fan-out requests? If you need steady qps consider our burst allowance or request an increased quota.

ash_customer: We have a small fan-out from a lambda that retries on 500s but not on 429s — could be accumulating. Will add a 100ms jitter and backoff on 429. For this ticket we want reproducible evidence for our security/compliance team. Can you produce a timeline of headers and timestamps for those three requests?

maria_sre: Will do. I'll produce a short timeline csv (timestamp, request-id, node, status, x-ratelimit-remaining). Expect in ~20min. Also sending the replay results once rjob_0042 completes.

sam_eng: After we confirm it's windowed rate limit we can offer two mitigations: (1) recommend client-level token quota increase, (2) suggest client-side pacing + retry-with-backoff. We should also evaluate if gateway's burst policy needs tuning for cust_42 if they're enterprise.

ash_customer: Thanks — attaching HAR and the tcpdump now to the ticket. Appreciate quick turnaround. :pray:

alex_support: Thanks all. Keeping ticket open — will post timeline and replay logs when available. :clock1:
